package view // import "github.com/geoffmilleraz/fathom/pkg/lang/view"

Package view answers span questions over a lang.Result: which symbol encloses
a line or a line range, which symbols a line range touches, and what bytes a
symbol's span holds in the caller's own source. It also nests a Result's symbols
into an outline of the file (Outline).

Provisional: fields and functions may change in a minor release until the LP-8
readings pass and one release has shipped (CH-D5). The package imports pkg/lang
and the standard library only. Its closure is pkg/lang's plus this package,
so a consumer of view links one package more than a consumer of pkg/lang alone.

A symbol has a known span when EndLine >= Line > 0. A symbol without one
is never guessed: a lookup the Result cannot decide answers StatusUnknown,
and a Touched set says it is incomplete. Nothing here reads a file or adds text
a Result does not already carry, except Slice, which returns the caller's own
bytes to the caller.

CONSTANTS

const RowsVersion = 1
    RowsVersion is the version of the row shape. Provisional (CH-D6).


FUNCTIONS

func Slice(src []byte, s lang.Symbol) ([]byte, bool)
    Slice returns the bytes of lines s.Line to s.EndLine of src, with their line
    endings, and false when the span is unknown or does not lie inside src.
    It reads nothing but src, and the returned slice shares src's memory.

func WriteJSONLines(w io.Writer, rows []Row) error
    WriteJSONLines writes each row as its MarshalJSON line followed by a
    newline: JSON Lines. It is what fathom-lang extract -rows prints.


TYPES

type FileRow struct {
	Error      string
	Dialect    string
	Language   string
	Skipped    string
	Level      string
	Incomplete bool
	HasResult  bool
	NullArrays []string
}
    FileRow is the per-file row: what the nested document holds for a file apart
    from its arrays, and what is needed to rebuild the nested entry exactly.
    HasResult is false when the nested entry's result is null (the file could
    not be read): its Error says why and the other fields are zero. NullArrays
    names the Result arrays that are null, not empty, in the nested document,
    from symbols, references, unresolved, facts and notes.

type HeaderRow struct {
	RowsVersion   int
	SchemaVersion int
}
    HeaderRow is the first row of an export.

type Index struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Index answers span lookups over one Result. It is immutable after NewIndex
    and safe for concurrent use. The zero Index holds no symbols and reads as
    incomplete: every answer is unknown.

func NewIndex(r lang.Result) *Index
    NewIndex builds the lookup once. It keeps copies of what it needs, so a
    later change to r by the caller changes no answer. Keys need not be unique:
    two symbols with the same Key and span are ordered by their other fields,
    so no input order changes an answer.

func (ix *Index) Enclosing(line int) (lang.Symbol, Status)
    Enclosing returns the innermost symbol whose known span holds line. It is
    EnclosingRange(line, line).

func (ix *Index) EnclosingRange(start, end int) (lang.Symbol, Status)
    EnclosingRange returns the innermost symbol whose known span holds every
    line of start..end: the latest Line, then the earliest EndLine, then the
    largest Key (the last symbol in listing order).

    The status is found only when the read is complete, a known span holds the
    whole range, and no symbol with an unknown span could be the innermost:
    none has a Line below 1, or a Line at or after the candidate's Line and
    at or before start. A symbol with an unknown span that starts before the
    candidate's Line can only be outer and does not block found. It is none only
    when the read is complete, no known span holds the range and no symbol with
    an unknown span starts at or before start, a Line below 1 counting as before
    start. Otherwise it is unknown, and the candidate (possibly the zero Symbol)
    is returned as a hint. A Skipped Result, start below 1 and end below start
    are unknown with the zero Symbol.

func (ix *Index) Touched(start, end int) (syms []lang.Symbol, complete bool)
    Touched returns every symbol whose known span intersects start..end, plus
    every symbol with an unknown span whose Line lies in the range, sorted by
    Line, then EndLine descending, then Key. complete is false when the read is
    Incomplete or Skipped, or a symbol with an unknown span starts before start
    (it may have reached into the range). start below 1 and end below start give
    an empty set and false.

type OutlineDoc struct {
	Path       string        `json:"path"`
	Dialect    string        `json:"dialect"`
	Language   string        `json:"language"`
	Level      string        `json:"level"`
	Skipped    string        `json:"skipped"`
	Incomplete bool          `json:"incomplete"`
	Nodes      []OutlineNode `json:"nodes"`
	Symbols    int           `json:"symbols"`
	References int           `json:"references"`
	Unresolved int           `json:"unresolved"`
	Facts      int           `json:"facts"`
	Notes      int           `json:"notes"`
	Omitted    int           `json:"omitted"`
}
    OutlineDoc is the shape of one file: its symbols nested by span containment.
    Every string is a field of the Result it came from, or the path the caller
    passed. The counts are those of the whole Result, not of what MaxNodes kept.
    Omitted is the number of nodes MaxNodes dropped.

func Outline(path string, r lang.Result, o OutlineOptions) OutlineDoc
    Outline nests the Result's symbols by span containment, the rule of
    contain.go: a node is a child of the innermost known-span symbol whose
    span holds its own, and among equal spans the first in listing order (Line,
    EndLine descending, Key) is the parent. A symbol without a known span is a
    top-level node with SpanKnown false. The input order of r.Symbols does not
    matter and r is not changed. An Incomplete or Skipped read still produces a
    document that says so.

func (d OutlineDoc) Text() string
    Text is the line-oriented form: a header, one line per node, two spaces of
    indent per depth, and a footer.

        # <path> dialect=<d> level=<l>[ incomplete][ skipped=<reason>]
        <indent><line>-<end or ?> <canonical or kind> <name>[  <signature>]
        # symbols=<n> references=<n> unresolved=<n> facts=<n> notes=<n>[ omitted=<n>]

    Every line ends with a newline. A string of the Result can span lines (a Go
    Signature keeps its raw newlines and tabs), so the text form writes each run
    of whitespace that holds a newline or CR as one space and drops such a run
    at either end of a string. A run without a newline is written as it is. Only
    Text does this: the nodes and the JSON form keep every string unchanged,
    so a node is always exactly one line and the outline holds one more line per
    node than it has nodes besides the header and the footer. The footer counts
    are those of the whole Result and omitted appears only when MaxNodes dropped
    nodes, so a truncated outline always says so on its last line.

type OutlineNode struct {
	Key       string        `json:"key"`
	Name      string        `json:"name"`
	Kind      string        `json:"kind"`
	Canonical string        `json:"canonical"`
	Signature string        `json:"signature"`
	Line      int           `json:"line"`
	EndLine   int           `json:"end_line"`
	SpanKnown bool          `json:"span_known"`
	Children  []OutlineNode `json:"children"`
}
    OutlineNode is one symbol. SpanKnown is false when the symbol has no
    known span (EndLine is then not an end). Children are the symbols its span
    strictly holds, never null.

type OutlineOptions struct {
	// MaxNodes is the most nodes the outline holds. 0 (or below) means no limit.
	MaxNodes int
}
    OutlineOptions bounds an outline.

type Row struct {
	Kind       RowKind
	Path       string
	I          int
	Header     HeaderRow
	File       FileRow
	Symbol     lang.Symbol
	Reference  lang.Reference
	Unresolved lang.Unresolved
	Fact       lang.Fact
	Note       string
}
    Row is one line of the row export. Kind says which of the other fields
    it holds: Header for KindHeader; Path and File for KindFile; Path, I and
    one of Symbol, Reference, Unresolved, Fact or Note for the rest. I is the
    zero-based position in the Result's array. Its JSON form is MarshalJSON's.

func Header(schemaVersion int) Row
    Header returns the first row of an export. schemaVersion is the
    schema_version of the nested extract document the rows mirror.

func Rows(path string, errText string, r lang.Result) []Row
    Rows returns the rows of one file: its file row, then its symbols,
    references, unresolved references, facts and notes, each in array order.
    errText is the error the nested document shows for the file. When it
    is not empty the file has no result: Rows returns the file row alone,
    with HasResult false, and ignores r. The rows hold copies of r's values,
    so a later change to r changes no row already returned.

func (r Row) MarshalJSON() ([]byte, error)
    MarshalJSON is the stable encoding of a row: one compact JSON object whose
    fields come in the order of the row kind's shape, with the same string
    escaping as the nested document. Equal rows give equal bytes.

type RowKind string
    RowKind names a kind of row. It is the value of a row's "row" field.

const (
	KindHeader     RowKind = "header"
	KindFile       RowKind = "file"
	KindSymbol     RowKind = "symbol"
	KindReference  RowKind = "reference"
	KindUnresolved RowKind = "unresolved"
	KindFact       RowKind = "fact"
	KindNote       RowKind = "note"
)
    The closed set of row kinds.

type Status string
    Status is the answer class of Enclosing and EnclosingRange.

const (
	// StatusFound: the returned symbol is the innermost one holding the line.
	StatusFound Status = "found"
	// StatusNone: no symbol holds the line, and the Result can say so.
	StatusNone Status = "none"
	// StatusUnknown: the Result cannot decide. The symbol returned, possibly the
	// zero Symbol, is a hint and not an answer.
	StatusUnknown Status = "unknown"
)
    The closed set of Status values.
